Generate an example SLURM array job script and handlers to run mechGEA on a SLURM HPC.

example_slurm_job.Rd

Please note: the resulting shell script, located in the output_dir named example_slurm_array_job.sh should be edited to fit the user's SLURM configuration. See notes at the top of the file!

Usage

example_slurm_job(
  beagle_files,
  sample_metadata,
  output_dir = ".",
  conda_env = "mechGEA",
  control_file_prefix = "./control/",
  env_mean_method = "unweighted",
  prune_r2 = 0.7,
  idp = 1,
  migration_results = NULL,
  memory = "100G",
  job_time = "1-24:00:00",
  cores = "40",
  setup_env = FALSE,
  setup_env_conda_path = "DEFAULT",
  ...
)

Arguments

beagle_files

vector of file paths to .beagle/.beagle.gz files to run. These will be formatted to phred files for running by the generated SLURM script for more effective parallelization.

sample_metadata

either a named list of data.frames containing the needed metadata in the correct format expected by mechGEA (see example_gl, although the $likelihoods object is not needed.) or an input sf object like sample_metadata.

output_dir

character, default ".". A path to the director where final mechGEA outputs will be stored in named sub-directories for each file in beagle_files.

conda_env

character, default mechGEA. A named conda environment to load at the start of the script. Note that if a conda module etc. needs to be loaded for this env to load, the resulting SLURM array-job shell script must be modified. See setup_mechGEA_env for help setting up a working conda environment.

control_file_prefix

character, default "./control/". A prefix indicating where the control files (including meta-data and the shell script) will be located. Either a directory ending in "/" or a file basename prefix.

env_mean_method

character, default "unweighted". Weighting scheme for mean envs if a sf object is provided to sample_metadata. See prepare_metadata for details and options.

prune_r2

numeric or FALSE, default 0.7. If numeric, the r2 by which to prune environmental variables to ensure all are uncorrelated. Scaling is always set to TRUE; to scale without pruning set prune_r2 to 1.

idp

integer, default 1. Inverse-distance weighting provided if using weighted env means. See prepare_metadata for details and options.

migration_results

file path or NULL, default NULL. If provided, mechGEA will use migration results in the list format produced by estimate_migration, saved as an RDS with saveRDS rather than re-running with the provided data. This is useful if you wish to assess migration once with a set of loci and then use that assessment for other genomic chunks (see stop_after_migration in mechGEA to estimate migration on one chunk and then stop the model).

memory

character, default "100G". Amount of memory to allocate to each job. See SLURM "–mem" option details for format.

job_time

character, default "1-24:00:00" (two days). Amount of time to allocate to each job. See SLURM "-t" option details for format.

cores

integer, default 40. Number of cores to allocate for each job. See SLURM "-n" option details.

setup_env

logical, default FALSE. If TRUE, will automatically attempt to setup a conda environment with the name given in conda_env using setup_mechGEA_env. If a conda environment with that name already exists, the user will be prompted to overwrite or the function will fail.

setup_env_conda_path

character, default "DEFAULT". Sets the path to the conda executable to use; see setup_mechGEA_env.

...

additional arguments passed to mechGEA.

Author

William Hemstrom

Examples

# first, chunk a beagle file
beagle <- system.file("extdata", "example.beagle.gz", package = "mechGEA")
chunks <- get_chunks(beagle, loci_per_chunk = 150)
#> Splitting into 10 files with approx. 150 snps per file.

# next, setup a conda env
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
setup_mechGEA_env("mechGEA")

# then, create the slurm job
slurm_script <- example_slurm_job(
  beagle_files = chunks,
  sample_metadata = sample_metadata, # the example metadata sf object
  conda_env = "mechGEA",
  control_file_prefix = "./control/",
  env_mean_method = "unweighted", # unweighted env averages
  prune_r2 = 0.7 # prune envs
  )

# lastly, edit the resulting slurm script with cluster/resource specific
# needs and submit the job.
} # }
